key_insight: MineNPC-Task provides a human-authored, machine-checkable benchmark that evaluates memory-aware, mixed-initiative LLM agents in open-world Minecraft using expert co-play-derived tasks, parametric templates with explicit preconditions and dependencies, and a bounded-knowledge policy to block out-of-world shortcuts.
problem_solved: Existing evaluations rely on synthetic prompts or permit shortcuts that do not test an agent's real-world memory, long-horizon planning, and mixed-initiative coordination in open-world environments; this work gives a grounded, reproducible suite to measure those capabilities.
method: Elicit tasks from formative and summative co-play with expert Minecraft players to capture realistic, human-like objectives.
Normalize tasks into parametric templates with explicit preconditions and dependency structure to support systematic generation and compositional evaluation.
Pair tasks with machine-checkable validators and impose a bounded-knowledge policy that forbids out-of-world shortcuts, ensuring evaluations reflect in-world sensing and memory limits.
impact: Enables AI/ML practitioners to benchmark and iterate on memory-augmented and mixed-initiative agents in a realistic open-world setting, improving the rigor and ecological validity of agent evaluation and development.
